verdict: Marriott's hotel fees jumped 14% as room rates and occupancy rose worldwide, lifting net income 9% to $794M — even though most of its $7.0B of revenue is pass-through money it handles for hotel owners.

kpis.label: Worldwide RevPAR
kpis.note: revenue per available room, on higher rates and occupancy

segments.name: Net fee revenues
segments.note: Fees hotels pay Marriott to use its brands and run their properties: $1,007M of franchise fees, $334M of base management fees and $181M of incentive fees, less $33M of contract amortization. This is the money Marriott actually earns.

segments.name: Owned, leased & other revenue
segments.note: Revenue from the small number of hotels Marriott owns or leases itself, plus other items.

segments.name: Cost reimbursement revenue
segments.note: Pass-through money: hotels Marriott manages reimburse it for costs it pays on their behalf — mostly staff wages at those hotels. It is booked as revenue and almost entirely paid straight back out as reimbursed expenses.

opex.name: General and administrative
opex.note: Running the corporate side of the world's largest hotel company.

opex.name: Depreciation, amortization & other
opex.note: Wearing-out cost of Marriott's own assets and systems.

otherDetail: Interest expense of $227M, partly offset by $8M of interest income and $4M of gains and other income; equity in earnings of $1M is shown on its own line in the flow data.

takeaways.title: Fees are the business
takeaways.text: Net fee revenue rose 14% to $1.5B — franchise fees alone were $1.0B, up 15%. Marriott mostly collects tolls on other people's hotels rather than owning them.

takeaways.title: Hotels were fuller and pricier
takeaways.text: Worldwide revenue per available room rose 6.5% — up 7.4% in the U.S. & Canada and 4.4% internationally. Net rooms grew 4.6% year over year, with a record pipeline of 634,000 rooms.

takeaways.title: Buybacks shrink the share count
takeaways.text: Marriott repurchased 3.5 million shares for $1.3B in the quarter and has returned about $4.0B to shareholders so far this year — one reason EPS grew 14% while net income grew 9%.

footerNote: For a hotel manager, 'cost of revenue' here combines the $5,067M of reimbursed expenses (costs paid on hotel owners' behalf, matching the pass-through revenue) with $395M of owned, leased and other expense. Marriott's own profit comes overwhelmingly from the $1.5B fee stream.
